ops.oldText: EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES.
ops.newText: EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO EXCLUDED CLAIMS, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE GREATER OF (A) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE TO CONTRACTOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS; COMPANY'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE TREATED AS DAMAGES SUBJECT TO ANY CAP IN THIS PARAGRAPH.

input.comment: [Playbook] We tied Contractor's cap to the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and replaced the cross-reference to Paragraph 9 (independent contractor status) with a defined set of Excluded Claims, so that confidentiality, data protection, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap. Our position is a meaningful cap with these standard carve-outs; we can accept a straight twelve months' fees cap as a fallback if the USD floor is an issue.
input.summary: Set Contractor's cap at greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1m and add standard uncapped carve-outs (Excluded Claims).
